name: Frankenstein's Monster
description: The tragic creature created by Dr. Victor Frankenstein

film.title: Frankenstein
film.note: The opening credits listed the Monster's actor only as a question mark.

legend: In the rain-soaked summer of 1816, the 'year without a summer' after the eruption of Mount Tambora, Lord Byron challenged his guests at the Villa Diodati by Lake Geneva to write ghost stories. Eighteen-year-old Mary Godwin, soon to be Mary Shelley, produced the tale that became Frankenstein. It fed on the science of the day: experiments in galvanism, where electric current made the muscles of dead animals and even executed criminals twitch.

myths.explanation: Victor Frankenstein is the creator. Shelley never names the creature; he is called 'wretch', 'daemon' and 'creature'.

myths.claim: In the novel, the monster is brought to life by lightning.
myths.explanation: Shelley keeps the method vague: Victor infuses 'a spark of being'. The lightning-and-machinery spectacle belongs to the 1931 film.

myths.claim: The novel's monster is articulate and well read.
myths.explanation: He learns language by secretly watching a cottage family and reads Paradise Lost, Plutarch's Lives and The Sorrows of Young Werther.

myths.claim: Victor Frankenstein's assistant Igor appears in the novel.
myths.explanation: Victor works alone. The 1931 film gave him a hunchbacked helper named Fritz; Ygor was Bela Lugosi's character in Son of Frankenstein (1939).

quotes.text: I beheld the wretch—the miserable monster whom I had created.
quotes.speaker: Victor Frankenstein

quotes.text: I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend.
quotes.speaker: The Creature

quotes.text: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.
quotes.speaker: The Creature

legacy: Son of Frankenstein (1939), Karloff's last full performance as the Monster
The Ghost of Frankenstein (1942), with Lon Chaney Jr.
Frankenstein Meets the Wolf Man (1943), with Bela Lugosi as the Monster
facts: The creature is never named in the novel; Frankenstein is his creator
Victor gathers his materials from dissecting rooms and slaughterhouses
He teaches himself to speak and read by secretly watching a cottage family
Mary Shelley began the story at 18, during a ghost-story contest with Lord Byron
He demands that Victor build him a female companion
Boris Karloff was credited only as '?' in the film's opening titles
Jack Pierce's flat-topped head and neck electrodes defined the look for generations
hostIntro: Tonight we open the laboratory doors on a fellow stitched together from spare parts and bad decisions. Don't blame him, blame the doctor.
